title: Two-Stage Algal-Bacterial Consortium (ABC) Bioreactor for Yamuna River Wastewater Remediation
meta: IIT Delhi Changemakers Summer Bootcamp 2025 · Under Prof. Jay Dhariwal & Prof. Anushree Malik (CRDT)
description: Designed and operated a zero-aeration Algal-Bacterial Consortium (ABC) photobioreactor addressing Delhi's 170M+ tons/day untreated wastewater crisis (5,300% phosphate elevation above permissible limits). The two-stage system combines physical pre-filtration (gravel, sand, activated carbon, muslin cloth) with biological remediation using a symbiotic consortium of cyanobacteria, algae, and heterotrophic bacteria. Photosynthetic oxygen generation eliminated external mechanical aeration, achieving 40–60% energy savings over conventional activated sludge processes. Operated a 2L photobioreactor at ~8498 Lux and 60–80 RPM; prepared inoculum via centrifugation at 5000 RPM with moisture analysis (89.6%) targeting 1 g/L dry solids MLSS; quantified nutrient kinetics via UV-VIS spectrophotometry (Barton's reagent @470nm for phosphate, salicylic acid @410nm for nitrate with R² >0.99 calibration curves).
note: Featured in The Indian Express for sustainable river restoration; selected among top innovations for exhibition at the IIT Delhi Open House 2025 Makerspace Showcase (presented to 300+ attendees); received Letter of Appreciation from Prof. Jay Dhariwal.
